$comment: Inventory of every credential MimmoBook depends on, used by scripts/ci/secret-rotation.mjs to guide a rotation. No secret VALUES are ever stored here.

secrets.name: VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
secrets.label: Backend publishable key (and project URL)
secrets.blastRadius: Public booking pages, dashboard, all browser reads. Embedded in the published bundle.
steps: Ask the Lovable agent: "Rotate the backend API keys." The agent runs the rotate tool, which mints new keys and rewrites .env.
Confirm .env now holds the new VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and that no key value was printed into chat or logs.
Republish the app so the new key ships in the bundle. Until you republish, the live site keeps using the old key.
Load the published site and one tenant booking page; check there are no 401 responses from the backend.
Record the rotation in docs/key-rotation-schedule.md (date, reason, who, republished yes/no).

secrets.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
secrets.label: Backend service role key
secrets.blastRadius: Full database access, bypassing every access rule. Used by backend jobs and the live security test suites.
steps: Treat any exposure as SEV-2 and open an incident record per docs/incident-response.md.
Ask the Lovable agent: "Rotate the backend API keys." Service role and publishable keys rotate together.
Republish so server code picks up the new value.
Re-run the live security suites that need this key, so a stale copy is caught immediately.
Review recent access: check the audit log and the reservation access log for activity you cannot account for.
Record the rotation in docs/key-rotation-schedule.md.

secrets.name: LOVABLE_API_KEY
secrets.label: Lovable services key (AI and connector gateway)
secrets.blastRadius: Server-side calls to Lovable AI and to connected third-party services.
steps: Ask the Lovable agent: "Rotate the Lovable API key." It cannot be changed by hand.
Republish or restart server code so it loads the new value. The old key stops working within an hour.
Exercise one gateway-backed feature end to end and confirm no authorization error comes back.
Rotate at most once per failure; if the same error returns after a republish, contact support instead of rotating again.

secrets.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
secrets.label: Payment provider secret key
secrets.blastRadius: Subscription creation, billing portal, plan changes.
steps: In the payment provider dashboard, create a NEW secret key. Do not delete the old one yet.
Save the new value through the Lovable secret form (ask the agent to update the secret; never paste it into chat or into a file).
Republish so server code uses the new value.
Run one real subscription action (open the billing portal, or start a plan change) and confirm it succeeds.
Only then revoke the old key in the provider dashboard, and confirm nothing breaks afterwards.
If the old key was exposed, also review the provider's recent API logs for calls you did not make.

secrets.name: RESEND_API_KEY
secrets.label: Email delivery key
secrets.blastRadius: All guest and staff email: confirmations, reminders, reports, password flows.
steps: In the email provider dashboard, create a NEW key with sending permission only. Keep the old one active for now.
Save the new value through the Lovable secret form.
Republish, then send one test email (a booking acknowledgement to your own address).
Check the email log for a delivered status and no failures.
Revoke the old key in the provider dashboard.
If the old key was exposed, check the provider's send history for messages you did not send.

secrets.name: GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_API_KEY
secrets.label: Search Console connector credential
secrets.blastRadius: Search performance reporting only. No customer data.
steps: Connector credentials cannot be edited as secrets. Ask the agent to reconnect the Search Console connection, which replaces the credential.
Complete the sign-in flow in the card that appears.
Load the search reporting view and confirm data still loads.

secrets.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
secrets.label: Shared webhook signing secret (per provider)
secrets.blastRadius: Incoming provider callbacks. A mismatch makes callbacks fail signature checks and be rejected.
steps: Generate one strong random value yourself (a password manager, or: openssl rand -hex 32). A generated Lovable secret cannot be used here, because its value is never shown and the provider needs the same value.
Save it through the Lovable secret form.
Paste the SAME value into the provider's webhook settings.
Republish, then trigger a test callback from the provider and confirm it is accepted.
Never store this value in a file in the repository.

before: Decide whether this is routine rotation or a suspected exposure. A suspected exposure is an incident: open a record per docs/incident-response.md and set the severity before touching anything.
Note where the old value may have leaked (a log, a screenshot, a public repository, a chat message) so you can clean that up afterwards.
Check nobody else is mid-rotation on the same credential.
after: Confirm the old value no longer works, or is revoked at the provider.
Remove the leaked copy from wherever it appeared, and remember that a public repository needs history rewriting or the credential must be treated as burned.
Record date, reason, who rotated, and whether a republish happened, in docs/key-rotation-schedule.md.
If a security finding or issue tracked this exposure, close it with a note pointing at the rotation entry.
